summary: Power Grid Corporation of India Limited. SAUDAMINI, Plot No-2, Sector-29, Gurgaon-122 001 (Haryana). **...Petitioner** **For Petitioner** : Shri Saurabh Mishra, Advocate, MPPMCL Ms. Nishtha Goel, Advocate, MSEDCL Shri Angaru Naresh Kumar, PGCIL Shri Arjun Malhotra, PGCIL Shri Yogeshwar, CTUIL Ms. Priyansi Jadiya, CTUIL The instant petition has been filed by Power Grid Corporation of India Limited for determination of tariff under Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024 (hereinafter referred to as “the 2024 Tariff _(3) If the information furnished in the petition is in accordance with these regulations, the Commission may consider granting an interim tariff of up to ninety per cent (90%) of the tariff claimed in the case of a new generating station or unit thereof or transmission system, or element thereof during the first hearing of the application for billing purposes till the final tariff is determined by the Commission:”_ 4. In the instant case, the Petitioner has submitted the information required for the determination of the tariff of the transmission assets as specified in Regulation 10(3) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. The Petitioner has also issued Public Notice of this petition in the newspapers in accordance with Section 64(2) of the Electricity Act, 2003. No comments or suggestions have been received from the general public in response to the aforesaid notice published in the newspapers by the Petitioner. 5. Thus, the Petitioner has complied with the requirements under Regulation 10(3) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations and has also met the requirements under Section 64(2) of the Electricity Act, 2003. Further, the issue of the final tariff order in the matter may take some more time; therefore, we have decided to issue an interim tariff for the transmission assets under Regulation 10(3) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations for billing purposes, until the final order is issued. Concession Agreement with CTUIL. CEA vide letter dated 4.2.2022 conveyed the prior approval of the Government of India under Section 68(1) of the Electricity (Supply) Act, 2003, to the Petitioner’s Company for the installation of overhead transmission lines included in the Transmission Scheme. ## 9. The hearing in this matter was held on 3.12.2025, 13.1.2026 and 19.3.2026 and the order was reserved. 10. This order is issued considering the submissions made by the Petitioner in its Petition vide affidavit dated 17.6.2025 and Petitioner’s affidavits dated 1.12.2025, 9.12.2025, 22.12.2025, 9.1.2026 and MSEDCL’s (Respondent No. 2) reply vide affidavit dated 26.12.2025, MPPMCL’s (Respondent No. 1) reply vide affidavit dated 23.1.2026, CTUIL’s (Respondent No. 8) affidavit dated 2.1.2026 and 24.2.2026 and Petitioner’s rejoinder to MSEDCL and MPPMCL vide affidavit dated 12.1.2026 and 19.3.2026 respectively. 14. In support of the readiness and proposed COD of the Asset-2, the Petitioner has submitted the following details: 15. The Petitioner was directed, vide TV letter dated 28.11.2025, to submit the Completion Certificate from CTUIL as per the fourth proviso to Regulation 27(1)(c) of the 2023 IEGC Regulations. 16. In response, the Petitioner vide affidavit dated 1.12.2025 has submitted the Completion Certificate dated 3.7.2025 issued by CTUIL, and it is extracted as under: 22. MSEDCL, vide affidavit dated 26.12.2025, has submitted that the Petitioner’s reliance on Regulation 5 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations read with Regulation 27 of the 2023 IEGC Regulations is misconceived. MSEDCL has pointed out that the Petitioner itself has admitted that the requisite certificates, including the CTUIL completion certificate in respect of Asset-2, were yet to be received and would be submitted later. According to MSEDCL, approval of COD cannot be granted conditionally or subject to subsequent filing of mandatory certificates. MSEDCL has also submitted that the delay was caused by the Petitioner’s lack of proper planning, follow-up and application for land acquisition and, therefore, the claim deserves to be rejected after a prudence check. 24. MPPMCL vide affidavit dated 16.1.2026 has submitted that in case of Asset-2, the Petitioner has admitted that the associated downstream 220 kV system to be 32. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner as well as the contentions of MPPMCL and MSEDCL. It is observed that the Petitioner has subsequently submitted the CTUIL completion certificate dated 3.7.2025, as required under the 2023 IEGC regulations, in support of its claim for approval of the COD of Asset-2. 33. The Petitioner has claimed that the Petitioner implemented and has ‘idle charged’ Asset-2 due to the non-availability of the associated downstream system under the scope of GETCO. The Petitioner has submitted the completion certificate from the CTUIL, as required under the fourth proviso of Regulation 27(c)(i) of the 2023 IEGC Regulations, to show that the transmission system is complete as per the applicable CEA Standards. 36. In view of the above, the Commission is of the considered view that the Petitioner’s claim of deemed COD as on 20.3.2025 is not admissible. With the 39. After carrying out a preliminary prudence check of the AFC claimed by the Petitioner and taking into consideration the time overrun and cost over-run in case of Asset-1 and Asset-2, which will be dealt with in detail at the time of grant of the final tariff order, we approve interim tariff of 80% of the AFC claimed by the Petitioner for Asset-1 and Asset-2 from the date of COD to 31.3.2029 in terms of Regulation 10(3) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. 44. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and the Respondents. The Respondent’s contention that GETCO should bear the transmission charges for the period of delay in commissioning of the transmission assets under the scope of GETCO has become infructuous, as we have not approved the deemed COD of Asset2 as claimed by the Petitioner.
